Lemma
[superlevel sets of concave functions]

Source: petersen:page-0476 ↗ def:pet-ch12-totally-convex 1. ch12:12.4.5If $f:(M,g)\to \mathbb {R}$ is concave, meaning $\mathrm{Hess}\, f\le 0$ weakly everywhere, then every superlevel set $A=\{ x\in M\mid f(x)\ge a\} $ is totally convex.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch12-concave-superlevel-convex \sketch The restriction of a weakly concave function to any geodesic is concave. Its minimum on a compact segment occurs at an endpoint, so a segment whose endpoints satisfy $f\ge a$ remains in the superlevel set.

□
